title: Optimizing Legal Document Discovery with Kimi-K3-DSpark
business: Legal firms managing massive repositories of discovery documents requiring rapid semantic search and summarization.
problem: Standard inference latency on large-context models leads to significant bottlenecks when attorneys must query across million-token document sets, causing delays in case preparation.
solution: Kimi-K3-DSpark utilizes speculative decoding to accelerate inference by employing a lightweight draft model that predicts token sequences, which the larger Kimi-K3 target model then verifies in parallel, significantly reducing time-to-first-token and overall generation latency.
steps: Provision a high-memory GPU cluster capable of hosting the Kimi-K3 target model and the DSpark draft model simultaneously.
Configure the SGLang inference engine to load the Kimi-K3-DSpark weights as the speculative draft model.
Set the speculative-dspark-block-size to 7 to align with the draft model's optimized verification width.
Enable the DSPARK speculative algorithm within the SGLang serving command to initiate parallel draft verification.
Monitor the acceptance length metrics to ensure the draft model is effectively predicting tokens for the specific legal domain.
outcome: Improved throughput for complex, long-context legal queries, allowing attorneys to receive near-instant summaries of massive document archives.
limitation: The draft model may struggle with highly specialized legal jargon not captured during its distillation, which can be checked by monitoring the average token acceptance length during inference.
